# architecture-containers

Matches the containers view against the runtime products the repository builds and deploys. A new server, a missing native target, a wrong technology, or a source layer drawn as a runtime fails. The view comes from the model `architecture-contract` reads; this check adds no fields or columns.

## What ships

Each product is proved by a build target, an entry point, or a deploy file. A dependency manifest alone proves nothing, so a native app may keep another language's packages for lint and build tools. Build manifests are read even when `.gitattributes` marks them `linguist-generated`. Files under test or tool folders are source types, never products.

Each [language module](../../internal/lang/langs/langs.go) brings a runtime reader. Its `Runtime` documentation names the evidence it reads and the products it proves. It also names their container's technology and the platform services its sources use.

## What the view says

An owned container is a `Container`, `ContainerDb`, or `ContainerQueue` inside a boundary. A container owns a product when a path it names covers the product's folder, or when its name is the product's name. A trailing `*` in a path, such as `go/cmd/fitness-check-*`, names every sibling folder it matches. A path of `.` names the repo root, so it covers a product built from the root folder and no other.

A container also owns a package a code span or label names, or a path covering an entry point its reader lists. A description word counts only as the exact entry point, and trailing punctuation never counts.

External systems, `System_Ext` and `Container_Ext`, need no evidence. A platform service the code uses needs an external system whose name, technology, or description names it.

## Failures

Every error names the view line or the evidence line; an error about both names both.

- A product no owned container claims, naming its entry point, target, or deploy file.
- A product two containers claim.
- A `Container` that matches no product: by name, or through paths that hold only source layers.
- A container whose technology does not name its product's language.
- An owned store that names no schema, configuration, or source path.
- A platform service the code uses with no external system naming it.
- A target without a type, a target source folder that does not exist, or a manifest the check cannot parse.

## Runs

No architecture views means a pass with zero files; `filesChecked` counts the container views.

## Scope

A test, changelog or doc change cannot move the views. A scoped run with no changed view, requirement doc, product or tool source, manifest or `.gitattributes` passes with zero files. Every other run reads every view and every product, so a change on either side still meets the other.

## Requirements

[Requirement 0073](../../../docs/requirements/0073-checks-architecture-containers.md) has one installed-command test per acceptance.
